questions.q: Why does the capstone's evaluation set need to include a question the pipeline should honestly decline to answer?
options: Ragas requires at least one failing test case to compute scores
To check that the score_threshold abstention path actually fires on a genuinely out-of-scope question, not just that the pipeline answers well when it should
Because context_recall cannot be computed otherwise
To reduce the total number of embedding calls made during evaluation
questions.explain: An evaluation set built only from questions the pipeline already handles well wouldn't test whether the abstention path from Lesson 22 is actually working.

questions.q: Why does the evaluation run the real pipeline from Lesson 29 rather than using hand-written retrieved_contexts and response values?
options: Hand-written values would run faster
The Ragas library technically requires live API calls
Hand-written values are easier to average
The evaluation has to measure the pipeline's actual behavior, not a guess at what it might do
questions.explain: Running the real answer_question pipeline and capturing its actual retrieved context and response is what makes the evaluation meaningful — it measures reality, not an assumption.

questions.q: According to this lesson, what does a low context_precision score suggest you should check first?
options: The re-ranker's relevance_score threshold
The grounding instruction's exact wording
Whether retrieval is pulling in irrelevant chunks alongside the good ones — the score_threshold or chunk size
The embedding model's maximum context window
questions.explain: Low context precision specifically points at retrieval returning noise, which this lesson suggests investigating via the score_threshold or whether chunks are too large.

questions.q: In the worked tuning example, what combination of scores points at retrieval specifically, rather than generation?
options: Low faithfulness and low context_recall together
High faithfulness and low context_recall
Low faithfulness and high context_recall
High context_precision and low context_recall only when chunk_overlap is zero
questions.explain: Strong faithfulness means the model is using its context well; weak context_recall means the real answer wasn't retrieved in the first place — together, that isolates the problem to retrieval, not generation.

questions.q: Why does this lesson insist on re-running the same evaluation set after making a tuning change?
options: Because Ragas invalidates old results automatically after any code change
Because a change isn't considered done until the specific metric that flagged the problem is re-measured and confirmed to have improved
Because the evaluation set must be regenerated after every change
Because re-running always produces the same numbers as before
questions.explain: A tuning change is only validated by measuring its actual effect on the metric that originally flagged the problem, not by assuming it helped.
